# Design decisions

Each entry: the decision, why, and what would make us revisit it.

## D1. Native iPad app, iPadOS 17.0 minimum
SwiftUI + UIKit, PencilKit, PDFKit. iPadOS 17 gives the Observation framework, `ContentUnavailableView`
and modern PencilKit inks. Newer capabilities (Pencil Pro squeeze 17.5+, Translation framework 17.4+/18)
must sit behind `#available` checks with fallbacks. **Not yet re-verified against current Apple
documentation**: do that on the first Mac session and adjust the target if needed.

## D2. Project generated by XcodeGen
`project.yml` is the source of truth; `.xcodeproj` is generated. Chosen because the project was started
on a machine without Xcode, where a hand-written `.pbxproj` could not be validated.

## D3. Platform-neutral core package
`Packages/AgentNotesCore` depends on Foundation only: manifest model, codec/migrations, geometry,
templates, search normalization. It is unit-testable without a simulator and documents the contracts
an Android client must mirror. UIKit/PencilKit/PDFKit code stays in the app target.

## D4. Document = package directory; library index = SQLite (GRDB)
- Content lives in one directory per document (`<id>.agentnote`): `manifest.json`, original PDFs in
  `sources/`, one ink file per page in `ink/`. See [DATA_FORMAT.md](DATA_FORMAT.md).
- Organization (folders, favorites, trash, recents) lives in one SQLite database through GRDB.
  SQLite also gives FTS5 for Milestone B full-text search.
- The index is rebuildable: on launch, packages without an index row are re-indexed.
- Large binaries are never stored in the database.

## D5. Canonical page coordinates
Ink and all future annotations are stored in points with the origin at the top-left of the page as
displayed (crop box and rotation applied), y down. Zoom is a view transform only. Changing a template
never moves ink. `PDFPageGeometry` converts to and from PDF user space.

## D6. Ink engine: PencilKit, one PKDrawing per page
Native inks only (pen, pencil, marker) until a custom brush has a real implementation.
Per-page drawings keep pages independently reorderable and lazily loadable.
Trade-off: the ink payload is Apple's opaque `PKDrawing` format. An Android client cannot read it.
Before Android work, add a portable stroke export (points, pressure, tool) next to it and bump the
format version.

## D7. Saving
- Ink: debounced (0.8 s after the last change, 3 s maximum latency), written atomically per page on a
  background queue; flushed synchronously when the app leaves the foreground, on close, before
  export and before page duplication. A failed write stays pending and is retried.
- Manifest: atomic write on every structural change.
- New documents are assembled in a staging directory and moved into place in one step.
- No separate recovery journal yet: atomic per-file replacement means a crash leaves the previous
  version of at most one page.

## D8. Own toolbar instead of PKToolPicker
The product needs a compact customizable toolbar, and one tool state shared by many page canvases.
The toolbar sets `PKCanvasView.tool` on every loaded page.

## D9. Flattened PDF export
PDF page content and templates are redrawn as vector; ink is rasterized by PencilKit at 3x.
PencilKit has no public vector export. The UI labels this export "flattened"; the editable export is
the native package.

## D10. Backend (not started)
Planned: Supabase (Postgres with row-level security, Auth, Storage with signed short-lived URLs,
Edge Functions) plus a Postgres-backed job queue and worker for long AI operations. Reasons: one
maintained service covers auth, per-user authorization, private storage and SQL transactions for an
atomic usage ledger. Provider keys stay in server-side secrets. To be confirmed against current
Supabase documentation and pricing before implementation in Milestone C/E.

## D12. AI key on the owner's iPad (temporary exception to D10)
The owner asked for AI features before any backend exists and chose Claude (2026-11-17). For the
owner's personal testing build only, the owner's own Anthropic API key is pasted in Settings ▸ AI
Assistant and stored in the Keychain (this device only, not synced). It is never in the repository,
notebooks or logs. Spending is bounded by a daily request limit in the app and by the spending limit
the owner sets in the Anthropic console. Requests go straight to `api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`
(no Swift SDK exists). Before the app is offered to anyone else, requests must go through the
server in D10, with sign-in and per-user limits, and this path must be removed.

## D11. Honesty rules in the UI
Areas that are not built show `PlannedAreaView` ("Not available in this build"), never a mock screen.
Every visible button has behaviour.
